Quarta-feira, 17 de Abril de 2013 17:12:19 UTC+2, Ricardo Cruz escreveu:
Hi,
 
I am building a performance test tool, and now I am doing the report module, and for this porpose, I am using R.
One of the perfomance counters I need to report is the Transfer Rate (given by a unix tool called atopsar).
 
I get the data from, lets say, 3 diferent servers, and I join all in one big dataframe, with the following code:
 
# Get all the NET related files on the results directory:
atopNETFiles <- dir(path=testResultDir, pattern="atopNET_", full.names = TRUE, recursive = FALSE)
atopNETHeader <- c("TIME","INTERFACE","BUSY","I_PACK_PER_SEC","O_PACK_PER_SEC","I_KBYTE_PER_SEC","O_KBYTE_PER_SEC","I_MBPS","O_MBPS","MAX_MBPS_IF_","HOST")
# Load all the info to only one var (which I call netLog):
netLog <- NULL
for (f in atopNETFiles) {
  auxLog <- read.table(f, header=FALSE, col.names=atopNETHeader,as.is=c(1),comment.char="",fill=TRUE)
 
  auxLog$HOST = strsplit((strsplit(f,"atopNET_")[[1]][2]),"\\.mon")[[1]][1]
 
  netLog <- rbind(netLog, auxLog)
}
 
After this importing, I am looking to create a graph with 3 lines, one for each netLog$HOST (each machine), representing, for instance, I_KBYTE_PER_SEC along the time. However (and this is my main problem) I need that 3 lines stacked (the last one would give me the a visual representation of the total load in the system; of course I would filter for the correct interface, but that seems to be easier and out of this subjeect)
 
An example of such dataframe can be seen here:
> head(netLog[which(netLog$HOST == "172.30.6.51"),])
      TIME INTERFACE BUSY I_PACK_PER_SEC O_PACK_PER_SEC I_KBYTE_PER_SEC O_KBYTE_PER_SEC I_MBPS O_MBPS MAX_MBPS_IF_        HOST
1 02:46:10        lo    ?           18.6           18.6               2               2      0      0            0 172.30.6.51
2 02:46:10       en1   0%           12.9           20.7               2               2      0      0         1000 172.30.6.51
3 02:46:10       en2    ?            0.0            0.0               0               0      0      0            0 172.30.6.51

> head(netLog[which(netLog$HOST == "172.30.6.52"),])
         TIME INTERFACE BUSY I_PACK_PER_SEC O_PACK_PER_SEC I_KBYTE_PER_SEC O_KBYTE_PER_SEC I_MBPS O_MBPS MAX_MBPS_IF_        HOST
2390 02:46:11        lo    ?            3.6            3.6               1               1      0      0            0 172.30.6.52
2391 02:46:11       en6    ?            0.3            2.7               0               0      0      0            0 172.30.6.52
2392 02:46:11       en5    ?            4.2            0.1               0               0      0      0            0 172.30.6.52

> head(netLog[which(netLog$HOST == "172.30.6.53"),])
         TIME INTERFACE BUSY I_PACK_PER_SEC O_PACK_PER_SEC I_KBYTE_PER_SEC O_KBYTE_PER_SEC I_MBPS O_MBPS MAX_MBPS_IF_        HOST
4818 02:46:11        lo    ?            0.0            0.0               0               0      0      0            0 172.30.6.53
4819 02:46:11       en6    ?            0.3            0.1               0               0      0      0            0 172.30.6.53
4820 02:46:11       en5    ?            1.7            2.1               0               0      0      0            0 172.30.6.53

 

So, as you can see; the time ticks of each machine are not necessarly the same (I think it is here where my problem resides). If they would be the same, I could just sum up the values; but the number observations for each HOST is different, and the time values are different as welll; so I don't know how to solve this.
 
Any help would be very appreciated. Thanks a lot!
Best regards, Ricardo.
